reviews.title: Great case for a good price
reviews.comment: Excellent case. Glass side panel and Acrylic front panel. Lots of extra room to work in with plenty of options to route your cables through. Fans have adequate performance for a decent budget build. They are not completely silent but not loud at all. They run at approximately 1500rpm and it's enough that you do feel the air moving from the case. The aesthetics are great and easy to control. All the fans come connected to a single controller which can control the RGB with the default LED button or if you hold the button down for 5 seconds it will work with your other RGB settings in your lighting software like Aura or Mystic Light. If I had one complaint, it would be that the cables from the fans to controller do not come combed out, they are tangled and shoved inside, but for that being the only issue and easily manageable I don't think it is a problem. If you're working on the bottom of an ATX motherboard, you will have to remove the lower back 2 fans but it is simple to do. The magnetic dust filters are a nice addition as well, easily removed for cleaning and don't disrupt airflow too much. It came with all the necessary hardware but I did have to install the forward 3 stand offs for the ATX board. Case buttons and USB ports are good quality with decent cables that aren't too stiff or hard to work with. Overall, I am very happy with the purchase and the way my build turned out.
reviews.author: DD85

reviews.title: Amazing value for the case and fans
reviews.comment: Couple of things: 1) The 7 fan LEDs are controlled by a button on the case that changes color. I dont know if you can put it into a mode where the controller can be fed by a 3 pin ARGB header or not, I just simply picked a color and matched it to the SAMA L60 360mm AIO. UPDATE, hold the led button down for 5 seconds, that will tell the controller to use the ARGB port if you have it plugged into the MB. 2) After you install the MB, just the MB. Flip the case over and unscrew the 3 x 120mm fans on the bottom, let them hang. Continue to wire any items like your case system header, with the fans in place it will be near impossible with large hands. If you fiddle without taking out the fans it will probably take 20 minutes to plug things in. Spend the 2 minutes, remove the fans. do your work on the bottom of the MB and then put the fans back in. Outside of that everything is easy and there is a TON of room behind the MB to stuff cabling. I had 1 SAMA product before, a black widow 1000w PSU which I used a in test system and it was fine, worked, so I took a chance and bought this case, the 1000w PSU in white and a L60 360mm AIO all from SAMA. Everything works, no issues. I came from be quiet! products which are exceptional quality, and pretty pricey. But those cases dont speak to the 13 year old nerd in me. This case does. Only the side panel is glass, the front panel appears to be acrylic, other people have noted that its glass but I can see the waves in the plastic from the molding if I look at it down the barrel. Still looks great. Temps are super good, obvious this is a very positive pressure case, the bottom and side/vertical fans are intake, the rear and the aio are exhaust. I set the fans to 50% pwm and they are pretty silent.
reviews.author: Phillip

reviews.title: Great budget case, but expect to spend hours on cable management.
reviews.comment: pros: honestly, it was a great budget case, especially coming with all of the fans. I absolutely love the look. It’s very beautiful and very spacious to put figures. The airflow is really great too. cons: absolutely atrocious fan cable management and poor RGB hub. I honestly wish all the fans came uninstalled, Because in order to work in the case, you have to take them all off and I probably spent over an hour and a half redoing all of the fan cables. Also, I’d recommend getting your own RGB hub. The one that comes with the case is really cheap. overall, I definitely recommend it, even though it’s a headache, it’s very much worth it because it is a pretty high-quality case and comes with all the fans so you are saving a lot of money
reviews.author: Kitty Lover Needs

reviews.title: Great Product! Great Support!
reviews.comment: -After many years of using an ugly case that had sub-par airflow, I decided to get one that looks good and has good circulation. -I got the SAMA V60 in white and it looks incredible. It has very good airflow and awesome lighting and fans that come preinstalled and wired through a hub. -The interior is very spacious, and there is plenty of room to store excess cables in the back where they are not in the way or seen. -It was easy to set up and had all of the hardware/screws that I needed. -I had some minor difficulties with getting my RGB and fan speed controls to work through my MSI software at first, so I contacted customer support. The seller was super helpful and gave me detailed instructions on how to solve the issues on my end. Now, everything is working great! -In case anybody has the same issues I had: -make sure that you enable the PWM fan setting (Not DC) in your bios so that you can control fan speeds through your MoBo software. -If you can't control your ARGB fans through your software, press and hold the "LED" button on the front panel of the case. This will enable the ARGB controlling. -If you want a sleek-looking PC case with great product support at a good price, I highly recommend buying from SAMA. And no, I am not sponsored by them!
reviews.author: gabe

reviews.title: A good case
reviews.comment: Built my first PC recently and opted for the V60 by SAMA. The chassis itself is great; a lot of room to work with and the quality is there. It looks wonderful. My main complaint would be that ATX boards do work but are very close to the base. I, unfortunately, installed my motherboard prior to feeding cables under it and being lazy, I had to feed a couple of cables through the side as opposed to the cleaner option. Not deducting any point for that because, as stated, the ATX board *does* fit. The included fans work well, though the hub is affixed to the base in the back. The cables also looked like spaghetti and required being detangled then reconnected prior to working on everything else.
